briefFidelity: FAIL, and not narrowly. The brief's first sentence asks for a botanical ABSTRACTION, the suggestion of a frond unfurling, NEVER A LITERAL LEAF. Before reading it I wrote that this is 'unmistakably a picture OF something: a flower head seen from directly overhead - the chrysanthemum / aster / dandelion / cornflower family. Not abstract.' The work is not merely more literal than the brief allows, it is a different plant organ entirely: a rosette, not a frond. Second, the brief asks for the logic of growth, 'a stem that divides, and divides again, each division smaller and turned slightly from the last.' There is no stem and no division anywhere in the twelve. 1243682 and 1446330 are the most articulated tokens on the sheet and both are concentric rings of petals at fixed angular intervals with each ring rotated against the last - a rotational stamp array with no parent-child hierarchy, which is why 1985692 and 1991107 can be near-solid discs. A ring rotated from the previous ring is not a division smaller than its parent. Third, and flatly, the brief says 'Fine linework throughout, delicate rather than heavy' and 'the drawing carried in line rather than in mass.' There is not one line in this collection. Every mark on every seed is a filled opaque lozenge; 1985692, 1991107 and 1310661 are pure mass, and 1203347 and 1475115 resolve into a single green blob at the core. I described 'the inner mass becomes a flat cream blob' without having read the word mass in the brief. Fourth, the state direction is inverted: the brief wants stress to retract the form toward a bare armature, and 1283437 under stress GROWS an entire new outer ring of green blade petals, while 1243682 under stress opens its core into a larger green pinwheel. Stress adds material here. Only the palette clause and the 'generous emptiness' clause are met. Four of six requirements are absent or reversed, so the gate fails.
composition: One move, made twelve times. Every token is a centred, fully radially symmetric stamp floating in the middle of its tile with the frame entirely unused - no off-centre weight, no asymmetry, no edge play, nothing that acknowledges the rectangle. 1203347, 1310661, 1561509 and 1991107 are interchangeable in placement. Focal hierarchy exists only as centre-to-edge falloff: the green core reads first (strongest on 1203347, 1475115, 1733538), the cream mass second, the grey outer petals as a shadow ring. That falloff is deliberate and consistent, but it is the only compositional idea present, and the brief's 'generous emptiness around the form' is honoured on 1283437 and 1835793 while 1985692, 1991107 and 1243682 nearly fill their tiles and lose it.
collectionCoherence: The strongest axis. Laid out together the twelve read unambiguously as one project: same dead-centre placement, same radial symmetry, same tapered-lozenge vocabulary, same three colour families, same soft opacity layering, same black field. 1283437 (small tight button) and 1991107 (large dense disc) sit at opposite ends of the range and still obviously belong to the same plate set. The one strain is 1733538, a compact ragged green star with white flecks flung around it and almost no white petal mass - it reads closer to a splash or a moss rosette than to the flower head every other seed shows, and it is the only token I would question the membership of.
palette: Chosen, restrained, and the only clause of the brief the work delivers outright. Near-black charcoal ground, one cream/bone family carrying the mass, one neutral grey family sitting behind as cast shadow, one sage-olive accent at the core. That is moss and bone over a dark ground, exactly as asked. There is no hue contrast anywhere in the twelve, which is a decision rather than a limitation: the whole collection is value-driven. The ground supports rather than competes - the cream mass on 1985692 and 1991107 reads cleanly, and the grey outer ring on 1310661 and 1366079 separates from black without muddying. The green does real work on 1203347, 1475115 and 1733538 where it takes the whole core.
seedVariation: Genuine and well-judged in range, though it varies the wrong quantity. Scale runs from 1283437 and 1835793 at under half the tile to 1985692, 1991107 and 1243682 nearly filling it. Density runs from 1243682, open and spiky with wide black gaps between separated outer petals, to 1991107, a near-solid disc with no ground showing inside the head. Petal shape runs from the long needles of 1446330 and 1561509 to the broad blades of 1985692. Core weight runs from a small green eye on 1366079 to a dominant green mass on 1733538. Nothing here is one work at twelve rotations, and nothing has escaped the project. But the brief asked tokens to differ in HOW FAR THE GROWTH HAS GONE, and because no growth process is depicted these differences read as twelve flowers of different sizes, not as one form caught at twelve stages.
thumbnailSurvival: Partial, and uneven. At 120px 1283437 (small), 1835793 (small), 1243682 (open and spiky), 1733538 (green star) and 1203347 and 1475115 (big green cores) are each still identifiable. Three collapse into each other: 1366079, 1446330 and 1561509 are all just a medium spiky cream burst with grey outer petals and I cannot tell them apart. 1985692 and 1991107 are near-identical large dense cream discs. So roughly seven of twelve read as distinct things and five do not. Everything fine dies at browse size - the green flecks, the centre pip, the grey shadow layering all mush, and the inner mass flattens to a cream blob. The brief's 'fine linework, delicate rather than heavy' would have been destroyed at this size even if it had been attempted; the mass survives precisely because it is mass.
marketResponse: Visible on some seeds, near-invisible on others, and pointing the wrong way. Clearest is 1283437, which under stress grows a distinct outer ring of green blade petals around the white puffball and drops it again in recovery - unmistakable even at 120px. 1243682 under stress opens its core into a large green pinwheel and lightens its outer ring to cream. 1203347 parts its petals under stress and comes back fullest and greenest in recovery. But 1310661's three states are very close at 256 and I would not reliably separate them at 120, which is the size that matters. More seriously, the brief specifies that stress RETRACTS the form back toward a bare armature and recovery EXTENDS the branching and multiplies its divisions. What actually happens is that stress adds green and pushes petals outward - 1283437 and 1243682 both look livelier and healthier under stress than at neutral - and recovery adds opacity and density rather than any new divisions, because there are no divisions to multiply. The claimed change is not the delivered change.
tokenIdentity: Held cleanly, and this is the axis the work handles best after palette. 1203347 is the same object across all three states: same scale, same petal count, same green core, differing only in how far the petals part and how much green shows. 1243682 keeps its distinctive open spiky ring in all three frames. 1310661 keeps its grey-shadowed cream mass throughout. 1283437 is the only one that comes close to the line - its stress frame adds a ring of green blades the other two frames do not have - but the white puffball core is unchanged underneath and it still reads as the same token wearing a different state, not as a substitute work.
artifacts: Clean on the mechanical faults. No clipping anywhere: every head sits inside its tile with margin, nothing meets the viewBox edge, nothing is cut in half, including the largest tokens 1985692, 1991107 and 1243682. No vanished strokes. Overlaps are soft partial-opacity and read as intended layering rather than collision. Three smaller notes: the loose white flecks scattered outside the head on 1733538 read as stray noise rather than form and are the one place something looks like a mistake; the centres of 1283437 and 1835793 are slightly muddled clusters where the innermost petals pile up; and at 120px the inner mass of 1985692 and 1991107 goes to undifferentiated blob, which is a legibility loss rather than a defect.
reasoning: This is competent, coherent, tasteful work and it is not the work that was commissioned. The brief asked for a botanical abstraction - the suggestion of a frond unfurling, never a literal leaf - built on recursive branching, a stem dividing and dividing again, carried in fine line rather than mass, with stress retracting the form to a bare armature. Before I had read a word of it I described a literal top-down flower head from the chrysanthemum and aster family, built from concentric rings of filled petal shapes, entirely mass with no line anywhere, in which stress ADDS green material and grows new outer petals on 1283437 and 1243682. That is not a near miss on one clause. It is a different organ, a different generative logic, a different mark-making medium, and an inverted state direction, with only the moss-and-bone palette and the dark ground landing as asked. briefFidelity is a gate and it fails on four of six requirements, so the verdict is REFUSE regardless of the fact that collection coherence, palette and token identity are all genuinely strong and that the collection would look good hung on a wall. Passing it would be passing an accomplished answer to a brief nobody wrote.
wouldChange: Rebuild the generator around actual recursion rather than a radial ring array: one stem that bifurcates, each child shorter than its parent and rotated a fixed angle from it, recursing to a depth the seed controls - that alone converts the rosette into a frond and gives 'how far the growth has gone' a real quantity to vary across tokens, replacing the current scale-and-density variation between 1283437 and 1991107 with genuine depth variation. Replace every filled lozenge with a stroked path of small constant width so the drawing is carried in line, and let the black ground read through the form rather than only around it - the mass on 1985692 and 1991107 is exactly what the brief excluded. Then invert the state mapping: stress should prune branches back toward a bare armature, so the stress frame of 1283437 loses its outer generation instead of gaining a ring of green blades, and recovery should add a further generation of divisions rather than adding opacity as it does on 1203347. Keep the palette, the black ground and the generous margin unchanged - they are the parts that already answer the brief. Finally, once the form is line-based, re-check 1366079, 1446330 and 1561509 at 120px, because branching depth separates at browse size in a way that petal density did not.
